quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): group-wide product shipment volumes fell year on year, offset by price management (passing cost increases into selling prices) and regional productivity programs. Revenue JPY 1,359,611 million (+3.9%), core operating income JPY 203,084 million (+7.4%), operating income JPY 197,882 million (+19.3%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 123,891 million (+25.4%). No single external customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue JPY 1,359,611 million (+3.9%); core operating income JPY 203,084 million (+7.4%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 segments (revenue / segment profit = core operating income): Japan JPY 406,296 million (-0.9%) / JPY 54,182 million (+15.1%) - separated gas and LP gas volumes fell, while electronics equipment and construction revenue rose on progress of mid- to large-size projects and helped profit; US JPY 360,557 million (+0.1%) / JPY 52,914 million (-11.5%) - weak shipments, electronics equipment and construction revenue declined; Europe JPY 350,978 million (+6.8%) / JPY 70,426 million (+12.8%); Asia & Oceania JPY 208,452 million (+18.1%) / JPY 19,746 million (+31.2%) - electronic material gas shipment volumes are on a recovery trend and equipment and construction stayed firm, plus the Australian LP gas business acquired the previous year and the Oceania industrial gas business acquired this year; Thermos JPY 33,263 million (+2.1%) / JPY 6,511 million (+3.6%).
quarterly_data.figure: Asia & Oceania revenue JPY 208,452 million (+18.1%); Japan segment profit JPY 54,182 million (+15.1%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New medium-term plan 'Next Innovation 2030 - Evolving for the Future' (FY ending March 2027 to FY ending March 2030), set in March 2026. Targets for the final year (FY ending March 2030), in units of JPY 100 million: revenue 15,000-15,750 (FY2026 actual 13,596), core operating income 2,500-2,750 (actual 2,030), EBITDA 4,000-4,400 (actual 3,299); EBITDA margin at least 26.5% (actual 24.3%), net debt/EBITDA at most 1.5x (actual 2.37x), ROCE after tax at least 8.0% (actual 7.1%). The three priority strategies are stronger industrial gas profitability, expansion of the electronics business (global roll-out of total gas supply solutions, focused investment in advanced materials, entry into new regions) and creating future growth drivers. Management states that wider use of generative AI and other digital technology is creating medium- to long-term growth opportunities in its semiconductor / electronics market, while geopolitical risk such as the conflict in Iran is raising supply-chain risk.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2030 targets (JPY 100 million): revenue 15,000-15,750; core operating income 2,500-2,750

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D (annual securities report): the company is developing MoO2Cl2 as a next-generation metal wiring material and in FY2026 decided to invest in a new MoO2Cl2 production facility at Taiyo Nippon Sanso JFP's Mie plant; shipments are expected to start in October 2026, mainly as a replacement for tungsten used in NAND flash memory.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Electronics R&D (annual securities report): with Rasirc, Inc. the company demonstrated a good silicon nitride film by low-temperature thermal ALD at a process temperature of 450 degrees C using diiodosilane (DIS) with hydrazine; it is joining imec's industry-wide research program on reducing the environmental impact of semiconductor manufacturing; it will build an Electronics Advanced Materials Development Building, scheduled for completion in March 2027; it is developing a nitrogen generator (NGU) for semiconductor fabs that co-produces ultra-high-purity oxygen and argon; and it continues to roll out Rasirc's BRUTE Peroxide hydrogen peroxide source for leading-edge logic and DRAM in the US, Japan and Europe. Group R&D spending was JPY 5,741 million (Japan JPY 4,846 million, US JPY 678 million).
quarterly_data.figure: Development building completion March 2027; R&D JPY 5,741 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: US R&D at Matheson Tri-Gas's Advanced Technology Center in Longmont, Colorado (annual securities report): the main focus was purification processes for higher semiconductor purity - using its WF6 manufacturing capability and experience to convert low-grade HF into semiconductor-grade HF for cryogenic etch and clean uses; it completed a high-capacity fluorine abatement solution for several use cases including lithography; it evaluated new packaging for corrosive semiconductor gases, with ongoing tests expected to support introduction to customers next fiscal year; and it introduced test methods demonstrating purifier efficiency below one part per trillion for acidic, refractory and organic impurities.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Compound semiconductor equipment (annual securities report): Taiyo Nippon Sanso delivered an MOCVD system (SR2000HT-RR) to Visium (formerly Lit Thinking) for aluminum gallium nitride (AlGaN) used in UV optoelectronics and power electronics development; its MOCVD system (FR2000-OX) for gallium oxide (beta-Ga2O3) films was adopted by Lund University in Sweden, the first of its Group III sesquioxide crystal growth systems placed in Europe; and it delivered a nitride MOCVD system (SR4000HT-RR-LV) and an oxide HVPE system to Ohio State University.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Sanso Holdings annual securities report: FY2026 (06-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex (annual securities report): FY2026 capital expenditure (including intangibles) was JPY 133,171 million - Japan JPY 26,738 million, US JPY 43,768 million, Europe JPY 38,682 million, Asia & Oceania JPY 21,315 million, Thermos JPY 971 million. Major planned new facility: Nippon Gases Norge AS is building a new air separation unit at its Viganeset plant (Hjelmeland, Norway), total planned investment JPY 6,672 million (JPY 1,925 million already paid), started July 2025, completion scheduled for August 2027. On July 1, 2025 the group acquired Coregas Pty Ltd and three other companies - Wesfarmers Limited's industrial gas business in Australia and New Zealand - through NSC (Australia) Pty Ltd.
